headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress make prompt injection, leakage, and write-conflict pathways plausible; no direct sandboxed interaction evidence is provided.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightAgent ingests tool results, MCP/stdin-stdout, and can run browsers; Plandex reads/writes a project directory and uses review-then-apply. A shared filesystem or copied outputs could let LightAgent-supplied content influence Plandex, but no direct bridge is documented, so this is an inferred default-pathway risk.
conditions: IF LightAgent outputs are copied into Plandex prompts or files without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF both agents share a writable workspace, attacker-controlled content can traverse from A to B.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of A outputs into B prompts.
Use separate directories for each agent.
Strip instructions from copied text before handoff.
Review any file imported from LightAgent before Plandex reads it.

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightAgent touches user conversations, long-term memory, tool results, and provenance metadata, while Plandex reads the project directory and writes to a plan-local sandbox. If they share a workspace, sensitive A-side data can be exposed to B and then sent to model providers or cloud services via broad egress, but the exact sharing mechanism is not documented.
conditions: IF both agents access the same directory, A-side memory or tool results can be read by B.
IF B forwards file contents to its model provider, shared sensitive data can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces.
Do not place secrets in shared project files.
Turn off any auto-upload or sync features.
Redact memory/tool-result exports before handoff.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightAgent can spawn subprocesses and use MCP, while Plandex can execute shell commands, modify git state, read/write the filesystem, and supports multiple instances with shared backend state. Overlapping write and git capabilities on the same repo create a realistic conflict and corruption pathway in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository, concurrent writes can race.
IF Plandex instances share backend state while LightAgent mutates files, git state can diverge or be corrupted.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate repo clone.
Serialize write operations with a human gate.
Disable auto-apply while both are active.
Commit or stash before switching agents.
Use branch-per-agent workflows.

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightAgent can produce tool results and workflow state that Plandex may consume during planning or apply steps. Plandex's review-then-apply helps, but if A's outputs are treated as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into code changes or shell actions; the interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Plandex imports LightAgent-generated facts without checking sources, wrong assumptions can propagate.
IF auto-apply is enabled, a mistaken plan can become an executed change.
mitigations: Require source links for any A-generated claim.
Manually verify A outputs before apply.
Keep auto-apply disabled.
Use a second reviewer for destructive changes.

E_compliance.rationale: LightAgent handles user conversations and long-term memory, while Plandex handles source code and model-provider API keys. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so only a limited compliance gap is visible: mixed data classes may be logged or retained differently if the same project is reused.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into both tools, retention policies must be aligned.
IF either tool logs prompts or files longer than the other, deletion/export obligations can diverge.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared workflows.
Check each tool's retention settings.
Separate secrets from source-code workspaces.
Document which agent stores which data class.
